gen-dafont-woodgod-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Vintage and loud, with swollen strokes. Woodgod stakes out the top with a wide-channeled swagger, while Pilcrow Rounded keeps its curves open and its strokes smooth and unvarying beneath.
gen-dafont-woodgod-fs-quicksand: Quicksand has lowercase bowls round as blown glass bulbs, with terminals that finish well clear of the stem. Woodgod does the commanding, vintage shouting up top, while Quicksand just hums along below it in lines of identical thickness.
gen-dafont-woodgod-fs-roundo: Roundo reads smooth and geometric, bold throughout, with an n whose arch matches its stem. And Woodgod brings the tall, vintage command above it, which is what makes the two feel so deliberately mismatched.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-headland-one: Tall lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals gives Woodgod its commanding, vintage stance, while Headland One answers with a dignified, gently swelling text serif. They share a taste for tall, rounded forms.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-stack-sans-headlin: Stack Sans Headline draws a monoline skeleton with wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. But Woodgod is the louder voice, its commanding vintage letters sitting well above that quiet, round-pen steadiness.
gen-dafont-woodgod-roboto-slab: Woodgod comes in commanding and vintage, its bowls reached through wide channels and its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. And Roboto Slab holds the line beneath with precise, structured slab-serif texture and open throats.
gen-dafont-woodgod-sora: Sora draws its curves without any pressure swell, and its c and s stay widely parted, precise and geometric. Woodgod sits above with its vintage swagger.
gen-dafont-yeasty-flavors-fs-fira-sans: Capitals that blend right into the lowercase give Yeasty Flavors a compact, handcrafted skyline. It leans on gentle swells and curls, while Fira Sans keeps one stroke width and a larger x-height for the quiet work.
gen-dafont-yeasty-flavors-montserrat: Montserrat glides under the eye like wire, with oversized e and a counters and generous white space ahead of each curve. Yeasty Flavors is the closed, nostalgic one, curling nearly shut.
gen-dafont-yeasty-flavors-work-sans: Nostalgic, handcrafted letters with a gentle curl define Yeasty Flavors, its strokes swelling slightly on the bowls. Work Sans carries a long passage in a modern, open way, its c tips never creeping toward touching.
